resolutions.researcher_notes: Reused/re-verified leads from the deep-sweep audit shard's status_review; original current_ref (timesca.com/interfax.com/intellinews.com, the last malformed by a copy-paste URL concatenation) is dead so this is a fresh citation, not an archive rescue. Two independent Russian-language sources, both from mid/late-2026: a 22 Jun 2026 nCa (News Central Asia) survey of Turkmenistan's oil/gas sector states plainly 'хотя давно обсуждаемая четвертая ветка трубопровода (линия D) пока остается нереализованной' (Eng: 'although the long-discussed fourth pipeline branch [Line D] remains unimplemented') — a considered, current statement made in the same piece that covers other 2026 Turkmenistan energy deals, not a stale fact being repeated. A Jan-2026 LogiStan roundup of Central Asia-China economic events independently confirms: 'CNPC планирует запуск линии D газопровода... (Многострадальную ветку D обещали запустить ещё несколько лет назад, однако реализация проекта затягивается)' (Eng: 'CNPC plans to launch Line D... [the long-suffering Line D branch was promised to launch several years ago, however project implementation is dragging on]') — framed as a repeatedly-deferred promise, not an actual resumption. A third, English-language source (qazinform.com, undated, carried over from the deep-sweep shard) has Tajikistan's Energy Minister attributing the hold-up to unresolved inter-country gas-pricing. All three agree the line remains unbuilt/non-operational — 'shelved' is the correct current status, corroborated in the primary research language.

Searched Russian- and English-language coverage (own search plus the deep-sweep audit shard's prior English search) for any source tying StartYear1=2022 to Line D, specifically. None found. Fetched and read in full the two Russian sources used for the Status unit above (nCa 22 Jun 2026 survey; LogiStan Jan-2026 roundup) — both discuss Line D at length but neither names 2022 in connection with it; every '2022' string on the nCa page is WordPress archive-navigation sidebar noise (monthly post-count links), confirmed by direct string-context inspection, not a date claim about the pipeline. The audit shard's English-language search independently found the project's original CNPC-era target was end-2020/Jan-2020, that by ~2021 reporting already said 'no completion date has been set,' and that mid-2026 coverage still calls the line 'yet to be implemented' with no year attached. No replacement year is sourced either, so this is left UNRESOLVED per the no-fabrication rule rather than guessed or silently dropped; StartYear1=2022 itself looks like a stale/unsupported figure (Update should review, not this shard).

Not sourcing the recorded Owner2/Owner3 values as-is. Reusing the deep-sweep audit shard's attribution finding: Owner1 (Trans-Asia Gas Pipeline Co Ltd, a CNPC subsidiary) is independently confirmed, but Owner2 ('Turkmengaz') and Owner3 ('QazaqGaz') are not corroborated by any source found for Line D. Two independent sources (AidData's project-financing record and an Enerdata report on the 2014 JV agreement) instead identify the Tajikistan-section operating JV as a 50/50 partnership between the CNPC subsidiary and OJSC Tajiktransgaz — Tajiktransgaz is absent from the sheet's Owner columns entirely. QazaqGaz is geographically implausible for Line D specifically: Line D was purpose-built via Turkmenistan→Uzbekistan→Tajikistan→Kyrgyzstan→China precisely to bypass Kazakh transit; QazaqGaz's documented CAGP role is on the Kazakhstan-transit Lines A/B/C route instead. Per the 'support the recorded value, never a different one' rule, this is left UNRESOLVED rather than citing a source that would appear to validate Owner2/Owner3 as recorded; the correction (Owner2 → Tajiktransgaz) is a value change for Update to make, not this shard.
